shouldFix.title: appliesFindingsOf misdates the complete landing of G21FXV3-M1 as v4 even though the pinned v4 finding says v4 did not fully land it
shouldFix.claimUnderReview: The subject says 'Codex v3 used G21FXV3-M1, landed at v4' and 'Landed in this lineage at v4' while separately pinning v4 as a Split predecessor whose Codex review rejected it on G21FXV4-M1.
primaryEvidence: The pinned v4 Codex review at SHA-256 6d041af3... titles G21FXV4-M1: 'The remainder inventory still classifies non-object top level as CC-5 and therefore does not fully land G21FXV3-M1.' Its impact says v4's lineage disposition claiming the v3 finding landed is false, and its remedy requires a successor to remove the remainder label and recheck appliesFindingsOf as part of one consistent classification surface.

Frozen v4 still contains whatIsNotAuthored[16] = 'CC-5 non-object top level'. v5 is the first version that replaces it with 'rejected v3 RF-2 non-object-top-level payload; not a CC-5 member'. Thus v4 lands the active-catalog half, while v5 completes the finding across the remainder and lineage surface.

v5 correctly records G21FXV4-M1 as landed at v5 and correctly identifies frozen v4 as Split: Claude ACCEPT 0/0, Codex REJECT 1/0 G21FXV4-M1. Those statements conflict with the unqualified assertion that G21FXV3-M1 had already landed at v4.

The current v5 catalog, classification rule, summary, historical note, and remainder text are otherwise coherent: non-object top level is RF-2 but not CC-5, and neither v5 fixture contains the rejected payload.
shouldFix.impact: The current classification and fixture bytes are correct, so this does not reopen the CC-5 scope defect or misdirect future fixture authoring. It does make the frozen repair chronology false and can cause a lineage reader to treat split/rejected v4 as the version that completed a finding its own pinned review says remained open. Accurate appliesFindingsOf accounting matters for determining which successor actually discharged a prior review requirement. Because the defect is historical attribution rather than current class authority, payload construction, or remainder scope, it is SHOULD-FIX rather than MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.requiredRemedy: In a successor, change both unqualified 'landed at v4' statements for G21FXV3-M1 to say it was fully landed at v5, or state precisely that v4 removed the active catalog member and v5 completed the landing by repairing the remainder classification identified by G21FXV4-M1. Keep v3 and v4 frozen and Split, keep G21FXV4-M1 landed at v5, and preserve the current v5 fixture bytes, non-object classification rule, open leftover-design, and no-execution/no-SATISFIED standing.

Custody passes: the subject remains 32e8c360... mode 0444; the fixtures remain df3f6198... and 76cc5805... mode 0444; all 28 cited path/digest occurrences reproduce; v3 and v4 are accurately pinned as Split; HEAD and last heading remain D-244; required-now remains 28; protected files are unchanged; G21 was not executed. v5 substantively lands both prior classification findings: the active catalog contains only closed CC-5 members, and the historical non-object note explicitly says it is RF-2 and not CC-5. Correct the two historical attributions to v5, or distinguish v4's catalog half from v5's complete landing.
